issues.description: Check identity is inconsistent across PR title, directory/class name, and CHANGELOG.
issues.detail: Directory and class are compute_instance_single_network_interface while the PR title and description say multiple_network_interfaces; CHANGELOG and code disagree on framing (positive policy vs negative detector). A check whose name disagrees with what it detects is unreviewable and will mislead future maintainers. Pick one name and rename everything to match.

issues.description: GKE detection via instance.name.startswith('gke-') is a brittle string-prefix heuristic standing in for real metadata.
issues.detail: The MANUAL-vs-FAIL decision rides entirely on a user-controllable name prefix. Anyone can name a VM 'gke-foo' to silently escape FAIL, and real GKE nodes with custom prefixes get incorrectly FAILed. Use the goog-gke-node label, instance group membership, or other API-level signal — or drop the carve-out and rely on suppressions.

issues.description: Zero-NIC branch silently reports PASS instead of flagging the anomaly.
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0, status stays at the default PASS while status_extended says the instance has no NICs. A GCE instance with zero interfaces is either impossible or a data-fetch bug; certifying it as compliant conflates 'compliant' with 'unknown'. Make this MANUAL/INFO or filter such instances out before the predicate runs.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model drops accessConfigs/IP data that downstream multi-NIC checks will need.
issues.detail: _get_instances parses accessConfigs to compute public_ip, then constructs NetworkInterface objects that omit access configs, IP ranges, and aliasIpRanges — exactly the data most relevant to multi-NIC bridging risk. Either carry those facts on the model now or hold off adding fields until a consumer uses them.

issues.description: Metadata Notes promise NVA handling and tests under-cover the GKE MANUAL branch.
issues.detail: Metadata explicitly calls out network virtual appliances as a legitimate multi-NIC case, but the code only handles the gke- hack. Meanwhile the test file covers the easy single/two/three-NIC paths but appears to miss the load-bearing GKE MANUAL branch and the zero-NIC edge. Either document the limitation honestly and add tests for the advertised branches, or remove the asymmetry.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this patch is NEEDS-WORK. The dominant P0 issue is naming: the PR title, directory/class, and CHANGELOG disagree about whether this check enforces 'single' or detects 'multiple' NICs. Beyond that, the GKE carve-out uses a user-controllable name prefix instead of real instance metadata, the zero-NIC branch silently passes an impossible state, and the new NetworkInterface model drops the accessConfigs/IP data that motivated the check in the first place. The underlying logic is sound; the framing, signal selection, and model design need rework before landing.
